messages:
incident-bot: Pager: high error rate and GPU OOMs on prod-inference-us-west-2. Metric spikes: kv_cache_memory_util and continuous_batch_latency. Triggered for service=runtime-v2, cluster=gw-prod-3. Link: https://internal.monitoring/alerts/1798001234 :rotating_light:
oncall-eric: oncall here, looking. Seeing a lot of 500s in the router logs and repeated cuda malloc failures in the runtime logs. Attaching tail:```
runtime[pid=2245] ERROR: cuda out of memory when allocating 128MB (alloc failed)
runtime[pid=2245] ERROR: kv_cache: shard=7 entries=4.2M size_bytes=54GB frag_pct=78
batcher: batch_size=64 avg_latency_ms=3800
```
sre-maya: thanks. Are we seeing prefix cache blowups or kv eviction thrashing? frag_pct=78 looks bad.
eng-runtime-anna: We rolled a batching tweak 2 hours ago that bumped continuous_batch.max_tokens from 2048 -> 4096 for throughput experiments. That could increase KV footprint per request. I'm pulling canary logs.
oncall-eric: initial mitigation plan: (1) roll back continuous_batch.max_tokens to 2048 (2) force kv arena compaction on nodes (3) tighten batch size to 32 for prod until we stabilize. Any objections?
infra-bot: rolling restart already queued for gw-prod-3 if TTL exceeds 15m.
sre-maya: no objections. Let's do rollback first - it's low risk. Anna, can you push config?
eng-runtime-anna: pushing config change now to 2ndary group to validate, command:```
# change config in svc config store
redwoodctl config set runtime.batch.continuous_batch.max_tokens=2048 --env=prod
redwoodctl deploy-config runtime --target=gw-prod-3 --wait
```
eng-runtime-anna: patch applied to 20% of nodes, telemetry shows continuous_batch per-request token windows dropping. But we still have several nodes with high frag_pct.
oncall-eric: starting a graceful traffic-shift off three worst hosts (gw-prod-3-{12,14,18}) to reduce pressure.
sre-maya: executing kv arena reclaim on the three hosts. Command we use:```
# run in host namespace
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/kv_arena_compact -d '{"shard":7}'
# then a light restart of the runtime process
systemctl reload redwood-runtime
```
eng-runtime-anna: note: compaction triggers short CPU spike; keep it staggered by 30s.
customer-success-john: CS has a couple of customers reporting increased latency and 5xxs for embeddings and chat — two paying enterprise customers. I'm preparing a status update. Do we have ETA?
oncall-eric: ETA ~= 25-40m to get full compaction + config rollout. Immediate customer mitigation: route those customers to dedicated capacity (if they have it) or use region fallback. Can we snapshot which requests caused biggest KV growth?
eng-runtime-anna: yes, we have per-request KV delta logging. Querying top keys now; looks like a prompt-pattern with long context + repeated function-calls that massively increased KV write set. We'll produce a list.
sre-maya: after compaction and rollback, memory usage trending down on canaries. However several processes hit cuda OOM before we could drain them. We should mark these nodes for full restart and prevent immediate scheduling. I've set node drain flag on the three.
infra-bot: drain flag set: gw-prod-3-12, gw-prod-3-14, gw-prod-3-18. Autoscaler suspended for 10m.
eng-runtime-anna: mitigation hotfix proposal (short-lived): enable per-request kv_write_limit=8 and fall back to fallback-model when exceeded. Config snippet:```
# hotfix config
runtime.kv_limits.per_request_max_entries = 8
runtime.kv_fallback.policy = "fallback-to-smaller-model"
```
cto-oliver: I approve the fallback policy for an emergency window. Prioritize customer latency over full fidelity.
customer-success-john: sending interim status to customers: "We are seeing increased latency and intermittent errors due to an internal cache sizing regression. Engineers are rolling back a batch config and performing compaction; expected mitigation within 30-45 minutes. Will update in 20 minutes."
oncall-eric: ok compaction finished on node 12, memory dropped from 62GB->25GB, frag_pct went 78->22. Node rejoined. Node 14 compaction in progress.
sre-maya: after compaction we observed allocator fragmentation still high on node 14; repeated small allocations causing fragmentation. Trying ld_preload jemalloc on restarted process to see if allocation pattern improves. Command:```
LD_PRELOAD=/opt/jemalloc/lib/libjemalloc.so systemctl restart redwood-runtime
```
eng-runtime-anna: quick note: enabling jemalloc helped reduce fragmentation in test, but we need to validate Cuda/pytorch compat. Patch applied to node14 — monitoring.
eng-runtime-anna: logs from node14 after restart:```
runtime INFO: allocator backend=jemalloc enabled
runtime INFO: kv_arena: compaction completed shards=[3,7,9]
runtime WARN: one request exceeded kv_limits.per_request_max_entries, fallback triggered
```
customer-success-john: one customer confirmed improvement, latency down ~40% for their traffic.
sre-maya: we still have a small population of legacy GPUs where jemalloc caused a segfault in nightly test; we've excluded those hosts from the jemalloc rollout. Need postmortem to decide default allocator path per GPU driver version.
oncall-eric: current status: rollback completed across gw-prod-3; batch size limited to 32; per-request kv_limit in place; compaction done on problematic hosts; three nodes restarted with jemalloc where safe; customer impact reduced.
eng-runtime-anna: planned followups: (1) add telemetry alert for per-request kv delta (new metric) (2) add guardrail in deploy pipeline to disallow continuous_batch.max_tokens > 2048 on prod unless flagged (3) schedule allocator-defrag runbook and an arena tuning work item.
cto-oliver: escalate to infra + runtime owners for a 72hr action window. We need a root cause doc and rollback guard in CI.
customer-success-john: will keep customers updated and offer credits for affected windows.
sre-maya: assigning postmortem: anna + eric. Tagging severity: SEV2 (customer-visible errors, partial degradation).
oncall-eric: thanks everyone. I'll hand off to followup channel and demobilize the pager in 10m if no new recurrences. :thumbsup:
eng-runtime-anna: collecting per-request KV deltas and sample prompts, will upload to shared drive for the postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by oncall-eric at 1798001238, severity=SEV2, incident_id=INC-2026-179800.
